question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed signed incremental catalog protocol as part of the staged ClawHub feed stack after the prerequisite trust and sharded-consumer PRs land?
rationale: This is a new network trust and persisted-catalog capability, so maintainers must confirm the permanent producer/consumer contract and staged rollout before an implementation can be accepted.

options.title: Stage after prerequisites
options.body: Keep this PR open behind the trust and sharded-consumer PRs, then require deployed producer proof and an updated narrow diff.

options.title: Adopt a different feed contract
options.body: Pause this branch if maintainers want incremental catalog changes to use another transport, persistence model, or rollout boundary.

options.title: Defer incremental refresh
options.body: Close or park the proposal if full signed snapshots are the supported catalog-refresh strategy for now.

recommendation.title: Stage after prerequisites
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open behind the trust and sharded-consumer PRs, then require deployed producer proof and an updated narrow diff.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contributor across all three related signed-feed branches; final product approval still belongs to the repository’s protected-label review path.
